chunks.title: Roadmap: Gully L3
chunks.text: An Arbitrum chain (the stack formerly branded Orbit): Nitro, deployed with the Arbitrum chain SDK through the parent chain’s RollupCreator and TokenBridgeCreator, with the Gully stack attached on day one. Explorer: Chain Kit, our Blockscout fork, with its Arbitrum profile (CHAIN_TYPE=arbitrum, traces from the node’s debug API). Payments: Gully Pay native on the chain, with USDC and ETH as assets, verified on chain the way it is today. Interop: Hyperlane. A Mailbox on the L3, Warp Routes for USDC and ETH from Arbitrum One (and Base) into it, and our own validator and relayer. Analytics, alerts, Gully AI read it like any other chain. The chain id for the public chains is not chosen yet: 412346 is the fixed id of the dev node and will not be reused for a public chain. It will be registered in ethereum-lists/chains and the Hyperlane registry before the devnet opens.

chunks.title: Roadmap: Gully L3
chunks.text: Both Arbitrum One and Base have canonical RollupCreator factories, so either can be the parent. The spec recommends Arbitrum One: the tooling we forked, the Chain Kit profile, the tracker’s Robinhood Chain coverage and the Arbitrum ecosystem programs are all Arbitrum-shaped, and Base liquidity still reaches the L3 through a Base→L3 Warp Route and, later, the aggregators. The public devnet settles to Arbitrum Sepolia. The parent’s gas price is one input to what posting a batch costs. These are the base fees on the candidates right now, read from their public RPCs in your browser; a chain that cannot be read says so. The other input, the parent’s own L1 data component, varies with Ethereum blob prices and is not reported by any public RPC, so the spec asks for a real batch to be measured on each testnet before the decision is final.

chunks.title: Roadmap: Gully L3
chunks.text: Rollup (recommended) (Batches are posted to the parent chain as calldata or blobs. No extra infrastructure.): Security is the parent’s. Costs track the parent’s gas; for an L3 the parent is an L2, so already cheap. AnyTrust (A Data Availability Committee you run (one DA server per member) signs certificates; the batch poster posts the certificate. Falls back to posting full data if signatures do not arrive.): Lower DA fees, but N machines around the clock, and a committee run by one operator removes no trust. The devnet and the launch use Rollup mode. AnyTrust is reconsidered only if the batch poster’s measured spend on Arbitrum Sepolia, projected to production volume, exceeds the cost of a real committee.

chunks.title: Roadmap: Gully L3
chunks.text: ETH. A custom ERC-20 gas token is possible (18 decimals, no transfer fee, no rebasing, no transfer callbacks, already on the parent chain) but in Rollup mode it needs a fee token pricer contract supplying the ETH/token rate to reimburse the batch poster, and every wallet, bridge and aggregator must learn the token. Gully has no token, and the spec does not propose one.

chunks.title: Roadmap: Gully L3
chunks.text: Hyperlane is the interop layer for the Gully L3 when it launches, not before. LI.FI and Relay stay the swap and bridge aggregators for the chains Gully Pay offers today. What gets deployed on the L3 Mailbox (Dispatches and processes messages): One per chain, deployed with hyperlane core deploy. Default ISM (Verifies inbound messages): Devnet: a trusted-relayer ISM (testing). Public chain: a multisig ISM per origin; for messages from Arbitrum, the public Arbitrum validator set already in the registry. Merkle tree hook (Inserts each message into the tree validators sign): Default hook. Interchain gas paymaster (Senders pay the relayer in the origin chain’s gas): Gas oracle entries for Arbitrum One (and Base) kept current by us. Validator announce (Validators publish where their signatures live): One per chain. Nothing is deployed on Arbitrum One, Base or Arbitrum Sepolia: their Mailboxes already exist (addresses in the Hyperlane registry). Warp Routes A USDC route locks native USDC on Arbitrum One (collateral) and mints a synthetic USDC on the L3; Base can be added as a second collateral chain. An ETH route is the fast path beside the canonical bridge, whose withdrawals wait the parent’s challenge window. Route contracts are owned by the team multisig, never a server key. chunks.title: Roadmap: Gully L3
chunks.text: Native: the L3 joins the payment chains with ETH and the Warp Route USDC; verification is the same receipt-and-transfer check as today. Cross-chain in: a payer on Arbitrum One or Base sends into the USDC Warp Route with the merchant’s L3 address as recipient. The invoice shows settling until the Mailbox delivers on the L3; both transaction hashes are on the receipt. Cross-chain out: merchant payouts to Arbitrum One are Warp transfers paid for in L3 ETH, with the fee quoted before the merchant confirms. Fee splits (the merchant fee proxy) deploy unchanged.

chunks.title: Gully Pay merchant terms
chunks.text: These terms are an agreement between Gully Labs (“Gully Labs”, “we”) and the business that runs a store with Gully Pay (“Merchant”, “you”). You accept them when you tick “I agree” in the Merchant tab of the Gully Labs App, which records the version and the wallet that accepted.

chunks.title: Gully Pay merchant terms
chunks.text: 1.1 Access and use. While these terms are in force, you may use Gully Pay (the hosted checkout, pay links, invoices, the payments dashboard, webhooks and the related APIs and documentation, together the “Service”) to take payments for your own business. 1.2 Non-custodial. Payments go directly to your wallet. Gully Labs never holds your funds: each payment is a transfer from your customer’s wallet to the receiving wallet you set, in your customer’s own transaction. We never have your keys and cannot move, freeze, hold, reverse or refund a payment. The Service shows a checkout, gives a quote and reads the payment back from a public node of the chain. 1.3 Ownership. We keep all rights in the Service. You keep all rights in your store’s name, logo and content, and let us show them on your checkouts.

chunks.title: Gully Pay merchant terms
chunks.text: 2.1 Your workspace. You are responsible for everything done through your workspace and by its members, and for their compliance with these terms. Keep your wallets and sign-in secure, and tell us at hello@gullylabs.xyz at once if you suspect misuse. 2.2 Receiving wallets. You choose the receiving address on each chain and you are responsible for controlling it. We check the address’s checksum and, for a contract wallet, that it is deployed on that chain before the chain can take payments; we cannot check that you hold its keys. A payment sent to the address you set is final.

chunks.title: Gully Pay merchant terms
chunks.text: 3.1 You will not, and will not let anyone else: (i) reverse engineer or try to discover the source of the Service, except where the law forbids this restriction; (ii) resell or give others access to the Service apart from your customers paying you; (iii) test the security of, interfere with, overload or get around the limits of the Service; (iv) access accounts or data you are not authorised to access; (v) use the Service for any activity prohibited by law; or (vi) present a payment to an address other than your receiving wallet as a payment to you. 3.2 Prohibited businesses. You will not use the Service to sell or take payments for: anything illegal where you or your customer is; weapons, explosives or their parts; illegal drugs or drug paraphernalia; gambling, lotteries or betting without the licences the law requires; adult content involving minors or anyone without consent; counterfeit or stolen goods, or goods that infringe others’ rights; investment schemes, securities or financial products offered without the authorisations the law requires; money transmission or exchange services for others; mixers or other services meant to hide the source of funds; anything for or on behalf of a person or country under sanctions; or fraud, deceptive offers, pyramid schemes or ransoms.

chunks.title: Gully Pay merchant terms
chunks.text: Final on chain. Blockchain payments cannot be charged back. There is no card-style dispute process, and we cannot reverse a payment for you or for your customer. Refunds are yours. You decide your refund policy and make any refund from your own wallet. Questions about an order, a delivery or a refund go to you; your checkout shows your support email for this. You are the seller. Your goods and services, prices, receipts, delivery, warranties and any consumer-law duties are yours alone. What counts. A payment counts only when it sends your receiving wallet exactly the quoted amount, in the quoted asset, on the quoted chain, within the quote’s time, with the chain’s confirmations, and its transaction was never used before. A transfer to any other address never counts.

chunks.title: Gully Pay merchant terms
chunks.text: 5.1 Fees. You pay a transaction fee only: of each confirmed payment, at the payment’s quoted value in US dollars. There is no monthly fee and no set-up fee. Your workspace’s first of lifetime payment volume is fee-free; a payment that crosses it pays only on the part above it. Fees are in US dollars, exclude taxes and are not refundable once a statement is paid. We may change the fee or the allowance with at least 30 days’ notice in the Gully Labs App; a change applies only to payments confirmed after it takes effect. 5.2 Statements. Every Monday at 00:00 UTC we issue a statement for fees accrued and not yet billed, once they reach; smaller amounts roll into the next week. A statement is a Gully Labs invoice, payable in crypto through the Gully Pay checkout, and is due within days of issue. When a customer pays in a stablecoin from a connected wallet, the fee on that payment may instead be deducted at payment time, in the same transaction, through Request Network’s open-source fee contract (ERC20FeeProxy), which sends it straight to Gully Labs; a statement then bills only the fees not collected that way. 5.3 Disputes. If you disagree in good faith with a statement, tell us at hello@gullylabs.xyz before it is due and pay any undisputed part on time. We will work with you to resolve it within 15 days. 5.4 Taxes. You are responsible for all taxes on your sales, on the payments you receive and on our fees (including sales, use, VAT, GST and withholding), except for Gully Labs’ own income taxes. We do not collect, report or remit taxes for you.

chunks.title: Gully Pay merchant terms
chunks.text: 6.1 Unpaid statements. If a statement is unpaid days after it is issued, your store’s checkouts pause: payers see that the checkout is paused and no new payment can start. We tell you when the statement is issued, on day five and on day, in your activity log and on Telegram if your workspace linked a chat. Paying the statement resumes checkout at once. Payments already sent to your wallet are not affected. 6.2 Other grounds. We may also suspend your store or workspace, with or without notice, if you breach Section 3, use the Service in breach of these terms or in a way that materially harms the Service or others, or if the law or a sanctions rule requires it. We will try to tell you first when practical, and will reinstate access once you resolve the underlying issue.

You are responsible for keeping your signing secret private and for what your systems do with events.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: We collect as little as we can to run what you use, we don’t sell it, and we don’t use it for advertising. This page says what we collect, why, who else sees it and how long we keep it, product by product. It covers gullylabs.xyz, docs.gullylabs.xyz, the Gully Labs app at app.gullylabs.xyz, blog.gullylabs.xyz, analytics.gullylabs.xyz, the payment pages, Gully AI, and the @GullyLabsBot Telegram bot and its Mini App.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: Gully Labs (“we”, “us”) builds and runs these sites and services. We decide what personal data they collect and why, so we are responsible for it. If you run a Gully Pay store or use Gully Analytics on your own site, you are responsible for your own customers’ and visitors’ data, and we process it for you to provide the service. Questions or requests about your data: hello@gullylabs.xyz.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: Signing in with your wallet. The app signs you in with Sign-In with Ethereum: you sign a message, and no password or email is needed. We keep your wallet address, when you first and last signed in, and whether the account is blocked. Each sign-in creates a session that stores a hash of a random session id (never the id itself), when it was created, last used and expires, your browser’s user agent and which workspace you have open. We don’t store your IP address with your account or sessions. Workspaces and teams. A workspace’s name, its members’ wallet addresses and roles, who invited whom and when, and invites (an invite link is kept only as a hash). If you add them: a display name, an email address, notification choices, and company details (name, postal address, tax ID) for invoices. To show your ENS or Basename we look your address up through public Ethereum and Base nodes and keep the answer for 24 hours. An activity log records who changed what in the workspace (for example a key created or a plan paid), without IP addresses. API keys and usage. We keep a hash of each key (never the key itself), its prefix and name, and count requests per key: per hour by result and endpoint, per day, and the last 50 requests (time, method, path, status and response time). Anonymous requests are limited per IP address in memory only; we don’t store those IPs. Contact and waitlists. When you write to us through the contact form: your name, email, message, the kind of project and budget you pick. When you join a waitlist: your email and which list.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: Gully Analytics is our own, self-hosted fork of the open-source Umami analytics, at analytics.gullylabs.xyz. We use it on our own sites, and customers can use it on theirs. It sets no cookies. A visit is grouped by a hash of the site, your IP address, your browser and a salt that changes every month, so we can’t follow you from month to month. Your IP address is used to work out your country, region and city and is then dropped; it isn’t stored. We also record the page, referrer, browser, operating system, device type, screen size and language. On pages where you connect a wallet (the app and payment pages), it records wallet connects and disconnects, chain switches and transactions you send, with the chain and wallet type. By default the wallet address is stored only as a short hash (the first 16 characters of its SHA-256). That is pseudonymous, not anonymous: anyone who knows your address can compute the same hash. To opt out in a browser, set the local storage value umami.disabled to 1 for the site. If you sign up for Gully Analytics, we also keep your wallet address, your sites, your plan and trial dates, and monthly event counts. Your Umami password is never stored by us.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: When you ask Gully AI a question (on the site, in the app or with /ask in Telegram), we log the question, how long the answer was (not the answer itself), which sources and live tools it used, whether you were signed in, and a salted hash of your IP address, or of your Telegram chat id. If you rate an answer with a thumbs up or down, we keep the rating with the question and the same hash, so we know which docs to write. We keep questions and ratings for 90 days. To write the answer, the question, your last few messages in that conversation and the matching passages of our docs are sent to Anthropic (Claude). When semantic search is switched on, the question is also sent to Voyage AI to compare it with our docs. When you are signed in to the app (or ask in a private Telegram chat linked to your wallet), Gully AI can read your own workspace’s store, API usage and alerts to answer, read-only; it never sees another workspace. The app also remembers your recent questions in your own browser.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: Using @GullyLabsBot requires following the Gully Labs News channel; the bot checks this with Telegram and remembers the answer for up to 30 minutes, in memory only. If you link a chat to your wallet for alerts, we keep the chat id and type, the chat’s title (for a private chat, your first and last name and @username as Telegram gives them), your Telegram user id and when you linked it. Link codes are kept only as hashes and expire after 10 minutes. You can unlink at any time with /stop or in the bot’s settings. Bot records. For every chat that uses the bot we keep when it was first and last seen, its language, whether it is linked to a wallet, whether it follows the News channel, whether it has blocked the bot or switched announcements off, and how it found the bot. No names and no message text are kept in these records.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: the News channel, whether it has blocked the bot or switched announcements off, and how it found the bot. No names and no message text are kept in these records. Announcements. The bot sometimes sends news to chats chosen by those records (for example, linked chats, chats with alerts, followers of the News channel, a language, or chats active recently). For each announcement we keep, per recipient chat, whether it was delivered (with Telegram’s message id or error). Its buttons go through a link made for that recipient, so when you open one we record that this recipient opened it, once; we don’t record when, your IP address or your browser. Our operators see delivery and opens with chat ids shortened to their last 4 digits. Every announcement has a 🔕 Stop announcements button, and Settings switches them off and on again; that never affects your alerts. The Mini App checks Telegram’s signed launch data to know who you are and stores nothing: no cookie and no session.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: Scans. When your workspace runs an AI Security Scan we keep a record of it: the workspace, the wallet that started it, when, what was scanned (a contract address and chain, a GitHub repository and commit, or an uploaded file’s name and size), its price or invoice and its status. To run the scan we store the code on our server: the file you upload, the full text of the source files fetched from the chain’s explorer or GitHub or unpacked from your upload, the tools’ output, the AI’s findings and the report. For a web2 scan, files named.env are stored with the rest of the code but are never sent to the AI or the scanning tools. Please don’t upload secrets. Who sees it. Members of your workspace see its scans and reports; developers, admins and owners can start and cancel them. Gully Labs operators can see the list of scans (who started one, the target and its status). To review the code, the files in scope are sent to Anthropic (Claude) after common secret patterns (API keys, private-key blocks and similar) are replaced; that check works by pattern and can miss a secret. When our static-tools worker runs (it does not yet), it receives the code too, on our own servers. The contract address and chain are sent to Etherscan, Blockscout or Sourcify to fetch verified source, the repository and commit to GitHub, and for web2 scans the dependency list in package-lock.json to the npm registry.

Publishing. A workspace owner or admin can publish a finished report. It then becomes public: the target, the findings, file paths with their hashes, and any code comments the scan flagged as attempts to instruct the AI; draft proof-of-concept code and the workspace are left out. Search engines are asked not to index it unless the publisher allows it. Published reports count towards that contract’s Gully Score. Unpublishing takes the report off the site at once; the copy stays on our server, not shown. Security Review requests. When you ask for a quote we keep what you send (name, email, project, scope, repository, contract, company, timeline) and the signed-in wallet if there is one. The request also goes to our enquiries inbox and to our operators’ Telegram chat. Requests are limited per IP address and email in memory only; the IP is not stored.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: The request also goes to our enquiries inbox and to our operators’ Telegram chat. Requests are limited per IP address and email in memory only; the IP is not stored. Monitors. For each contract your workspace watches we keep the contract, chain and name, your alert thresholds, your webhook address and its signing secret, whether Telegram is on, whether the contract may be listed publicly, the contract’s last read state, its last 100 events and the last 50 alert deliveries. The contract is read through public blockchain nodes. Events a monitor sees are public chain data and count in that contract’s public Gully Score; switching listing off keeps the contract off the public list of scores, not out of its score.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: Holder Map. Looking up a map needs no account. To show the maps opened most today we count one view per visitor per token per day, using a hash of the IP address made with a random key that is held in memory only and replaced every day; the counts are reset each UTC day. New maps are limited per IP address for a minute, in memory only. To build a map we send the token’s address (never anything about you) to DeepCore, Blockscout, Moralis, Solana nodes and public blockchain nodes. Holder alerts are kept like other alerts, until you delete them. Gully Score. Looking up a score needs no account and we don’t record who looked. We keep each contract’s latest score and its history. The contract address is sent to Sourcify, Etherscan and public blockchain nodes to read its evidence. Lookups are limited per IP address in memory only.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: Payments happen on public blockchains. A transaction, the addresses in it and the amount are public and permanent, and nobody (us included) can change or delete them. We never hold your funds. When you pay us or a Gully Pay store, we record the transaction hash, chain, asset, amount, its US dollar value at the time, the paying address and the block, to confirm and receipt the payment. A store’s owner sees its own payments, and its webhook sends the payment, including the paying address, to the address the store sets. A store can put a customer name and email on an invoice; the store decides that, and is responsible for it. We count how often an invoice page is opened, without storing who opened it. For a store we keep its name, logo (copied once from the address given, never hot-linked), accent colour, support email, website, receiving wallets, which version of the merchant terms it accepted and with which wallet, its invoices, links, fees and statements.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: One cookie of ours: the app’s sign-in cookie (__Host-gl_dev), only after you sign in. It is HttpOnly, sent only to the app over HTTPS, and lasts 30 days or until you sign out. No advertising or cross-site tracking cookies, and Gully Analytics uses none. Browser storage remembers choices on your device only: the app’s sidebar, invites you declined, that you accepted the swap risk notice, recent Gully AI questions in the app, and requests you already sent (Chain Kit, devnet waitlist). The blog (Ghost) runs on our server and handles its own visitors; its member sign-up is switched off.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: We don’t sell personal data or share it for advertising. These services see some of it because they carry or power what you use: Cloudflare carries all traffic to our sites, so it sees your IP address and requests, and tells our server your country. Its Web Analytics beacon runs on our pages. Anthropic and, when switched on, Voyage AI: Gully AI questions, as above. Anthropic also reviews the code of Gully Security scans. Etherscan, Blockscout, Sourcify, GitHub and the npm registry: the contract, repository or dependency list a Gully Security scan or a Gully Score reads, as above. DeepCore, Blockscout and Moralis: token addresses for the Holder Map, as above. Telegram: everything you send to or receive from the bot. Blockchain node providers (public RPC endpoints): we read transactions, balances and ENS names through them, which can include your address. Your wallet talks to its own nodes. Wallet and swap services you choose to use: WalletConnect when you connect a wallet that way, LI.FI in the swap widget, and Jupiter for Solana swaps (it receives your public key). Addresses you give us: alert and store webhooks are sent to the URLs you set. We may disclose data when the law requires it, to protect our users or services from fraud or abuse, or to a buyer if Gully Labs is sold, under this policy.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: Sessions last 30 days. Gully AI questions and ratings are kept 90 days. The activity log keeps 180 days, and so does a security scan’s code. Backups are kept 7 days. Accounts, payments and stores are not deleted automatically today. Sign-in sessions: 30 days from sign-in (at most 20 per wallet), or until you sign out or revoke them. Team invites: 7 days to accept; closed invites are deleted 30 days after they close. Workspace activity log: The newest 1,000 events, none older than 180 days. API usage counts per key: Hourly counts 31 days; the last 50 requests and daily totals until the key or account is deleted. Gully AI questions and ratings: 90 days. Telegram link codes: 10 minutes to use; deleted a day after they expire. Unpaid payment quotes: Deleted 7 days after they expire. Webhook deliveries: The newest 1,000 for Gully Pay; the newest 50 per gap alert. Contact form messages: The newest 5,000 messages. Security scans: the code, the fetched sources, tool output and the report: Deleted once the scan is finished and 180 days old, when our server next restarts after that; the scan’s entry in your list (without the code) is not deleted automatically. Code uploaded for a scan: Moved into the scan when it starts; deleted at once if a free scan cannot start or you cancel an unpaid scan; the upload of a paid scan left unpaid stays until you cancel it.

chunks.text: it starts; deleted at once if a free scan cannot start or you cancel an unpaid scan; the upload of a paid scan left unpaid stays until you cancel it. Published scan reports: Public until unpublished; after that the copy stays on our server, not shown, and is not deleted automatically. Security Review requests: The newest 5,000 requests. Security monitors: Until you delete the monitor; each keeps its last 100 events and last 50 alert deliveries. Gully Score results and history: Not deleted automatically (who looked a score up is not recorded). Holder Map view counts: Reset every UTC day; the key that hashes visitors is never written down. Telegram announcements: deliveries and opened links: The newest 200 announcements. Telegram bot records (first and last seen, language, opt-out): Not deleted automatically today. Backups of all of the above: 7 days. Accounts, workspaces, keys, payments, invoices, stores, Telegram links, waitlists, analytics data: Not deleted automatically today; ask us and we delete what the law lets us.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: We store hashes instead of secrets wherever we can (session ids, API keys, invite and link codes, IP addresses in the Gully AI log and the Holder Map counts), use HTTPS everywhere, and back the data up every night to the same server, keeping 7 days. No system is perfectly secure; if a breach affects your data, we will tell you as the law requires.

chunks.title: Privacy policy
chunks.text: Sign out, or revoke any session, in the app’s Settings. Revoke API keys, delete alerts, remove webhooks and switch off pay links in the app. Unlink Telegram with /stop or in the bot’s settings, and switch announcements off with 🔕 Stop announcements or in Settings. Delete a monitor, or unpublish a scan report, in the app; ask us to delete a scan’s code before the 180 days are up. Opt out of Gully Analytics as described above, or use a browser that blocks scripts. Ask us at hello@gullylabs.xyz to see, correct, export or delete what we hold about you off-chain. The app doesn’t have a self-service “delete my account” button yet, so email us and we will do it. We may keep payment records where the law requires, and we can’t delete anything that is on a public blockchain. Depending on where you live, you may also have the right to object to or restrict how we use your data, and to complain to your data protection authority. Our services are not meant for anyone under 18.

chunks.title: Privacy policy

chunks.section: Gully Pay fee split: which existing contract
chunks.text: *Question. Which existing contract, already deployed, can pay the merchant and send the Gully Labs fee to the treasury in one transaction, without custody? *Answer. Use Request Network's ERC20FeeProxy for tokens (USDC and USDT) on Base, Ethereum, BNB Chain and Arbitrum, and since 2026-10-18 on OP Mainnet too, whose proxy is byte-identical to Base's (section "Chains added 2026-10-18" below). Keep native coin (ETH, BNB, POL, AVAX), Polygon, Avalanche and Robinhood Chain on plain transfers, with the fee invoiced as it is today. Gully Labs deploys nothing, and the custom splitter on this branch has been deleted. Checked on 2026-10-17. Every address was read with eth_getCode through the same public RPCs that server/payments.mjs uses.

chunks.title: Gully Pay fee split: which contract and why

chunks.title: Roadmap: the Gully L3 spec
chunks.text: From the Arbitrum docs (choose AnyTrust and Inside AnyTrust, read 2026-10-17): Rollup: "Transaction data is posted to the parent chain as calldata or blobs", DataAvailabilityCommittee: false, "No additional steps are required." Security is the parent's. AnyTrust: a Data Availability Committee "which is a group of permissioned nodes that you choose and run, or outsource to a Rollup-as-a-Service (RaaS)". The batch poster posts a DACert "signed by the required number of DAC members (configurable)"; with N members the certificate needs N-1 signatures and the assumption is that "at least two are honest". If the sequencer cannot collect enough signatures "within a few minutes" it posts the full data to the parent chain instead (rollup fallback). Setup: "Deploy a Data Availability Server (DAS) for each DAC member", generate a BLS keyset, register it on SequencerInbox. Costs: The Arbitrum docs give no figure for either mode; they say the parent-chain data posting is "the largest component of the cost of using Arbitrum". For an L3 the parent is itself an L2, whose calldata is already cheap (base fees of 0.005 to 0.02 gwei measured above, plus the L2's own L1 data component). AnyTrust adds machines: one DAS per committee member, around the clock, plus mirrors. A committee run entirely by us has N members but one operator, so it removes no trust; it only cuts DA fees. *Recommendation: Rollup (D2) for S1 and the launch. Measure the batch poster's monthly spend on Arbitrum Sepolia during S1; switch to AnyTrust only if that spend, projected to S2 volume, exceeds the cost of running a real committee (at least four DAS machines plus a second operator).

chunks.title: Roadmap: the Gully L3 spec
chunks.text: Options and their rules (Arbitrum docs, choose a custom gas token and the custom gas token on AnyTrust page, 2026-10-17): ETH (default): nothing to configure; wallets, LI.FI, Relay and Hyperlane's gas oracles all understand it; Gully Pay already prices ETH with the same-chain Chainlink feed. Custom ERC-20: "Must be a standard ERC-20 token", "Must not be rebasing or include transfer fees", transfers and approvals "must occur directly via the token contract, not via proxies or hooks", no transfer callbacks; 18 decimals (SDK guides). It must already exist on the parent chain and is "natively bridged" at deployment. In Rollup mode the batch poster is reimbursed in the fee token, so a fee token pricer contract supplying the ETH/token exchange rate must be deployed and registered on the parent; the docs' three examples are marked as not for production and "If the fee token pricer returns stale or manipulated prices, the batch poster may be under- or over-reimbursed." On AnyTrust the chain owner must also call SetL1PricePerUnit(0) and SetL1PricingRewardRate(0) or "Nitro will apply a parent chain's fee to all transactions". *Recommendation: ETH (D3). Gully has no token; a gas token would be a new product with its own risks (the pricer, liquidity, listings). If the owner wants a Gully gas token later, it is a new chain parameter at deployment time, not a switch.

chunks.title: Roadmap: the Gully L3 spec
chunks.text: Chain Kit (our Blockscout fork) joins the chain's compose network and indexes the RPC with CHAIN_ID, CHAIN_TYPE=arbitrum, ETHEREUM_JSONRPC_VARIANT=geth, ETHEREUM_JSONRPC_TRACE_URL (the node exposes debug). Stack: Postgres, backend, frontend, Redis: "several GB of images and 1 to 2 GB of RAM" (devnet README), so its own compose project and disk check. Served through gully-web on explorer.devnet.gullylabs.xyz (S1) and explorer.gullylabs.xyz (S2) the way the blog is forwarded (server/blog.mjs), never on a public host port. Hyperlane messages are shown by Hyperlane's own explorer once the chain is in the registry; Chain Kit shows the Mailbox Dispatch/Process events like any contract.

chunks.title: Roadmap: the Gully L3 spec
chunks.text: A gully-web route (POST /api/devnet/faucet) that sends a fixed amount of the L3's ETH from a faucet key held in .env, rate-limited per address and IP, after the same Turnstile the contact form uses. The faucet key is funded through the canonical bridge from Arbitrum Sepolia ETH (public faucets). The Devnet waitlist (/api/notify, slot 90) is the first audience. On S0 (--dev) the pre-funded dev account funds the faucet key; its private key is public (nitro-devnode README), so the S0 RPC is never exposed.

chunks.title: Roadmap: the Gully L3 spec
chunks.text: S1/S2: rpc.devnet.gullylabs.xyz / rpc.gullylabs.xyz, forwarded by gully-web to the full node, with the eth, net, web3 namespaces only and debug kept for Chain Kit on the internal network. Hyperlane's validator docs say "You must use your own RPC urls not any public ones": the agents read our node on the internal network, never the public host. Metadata for wallets: chain id, ETH, explorer URL, in ethereum-lists/chains and in the Hyperlane registry (metadata.yaml), both PRs at S1.

chunks.title: Roadmap: the Gully L3 spec
chunks.text: Owner decision (2026-10-17): Hyperlane is the interop layer for the Gully L3 when it launches, not before. Until then LI.FI and Relay stay the swap and bridge aggregators for the chains Gully Pay offers today (Base, Ethereum, BNB Chain, Arbitrum One, plus Solana where the site offers it).
